name: Strike Lab - Fighting Game Training Arena
request: Create a small, playable Strike Lab fighting-game training arena for one player on desktop and touch. Include a humanoid training dummy, a three-hit light-attack combo with visible windup, contact and recovery animations, synchronized hit sound effects, a visible accepted-hit counter and dummy health. The server must validate attack timing and range. Each accepted strike damages and counts once at contact; swinging out of range, holding the button or spamming during recovery must not create extra hits. Show distinct hit and miss feedback. After defeat, reset the dummy and let the player practice again; provide a clear reset control and an uncluttered arena. Search Marketplace first for complete reusable combat/training components, compatible dummy rigs, existing animations and sound rather than rebuilding everything. Inspect compatibility, behavior and included media, preserve useful working pieces and author only missing integration. Source missing audio from Marketplace and verify actual playing animations and audible sounds. Record an importer capability gap honestly rather than treating it as a bad asset. Choose reasonable styling and damage values yourself. No PvP, matchmaking, saving, monetization or large world. Success needs native evidence for the full combo, exact counting, misses, recovery spam, defeat/reset and desktop/touch controls. A damage script with a static dummy does not meet the animation requirement.

assetNeeds.role: Impact sound effect for accepted strikes
assetNeeds.constraints: Clear, punchy combat hit sound effect under 2 seconds, no silence at start

intent.experienceRole: Gives immediate, satisfying auditory confirmation for successful strike contact.
intent.interaction: Plays on dummy or character whenever server confirms an accepted hit.

assetNeeds.role: Swing whoosh audio effect for attack windup/miss
assetNeeds.constraints: Fast, clean air whoosh combat sound under 1.5 seconds

intent.experienceRole: Provides auditory anticipation during attack windup and distinct feedback for whiffed/missed attacks.
intent.interaction: Plays immediately when the player initiates a strike swing.

spec.assetStrategy: Search Marketplace for a humanoid training dummy model/rig, punch/kick hit sound effects, and melee swing/whoosh audio. Rig animations or procedural joint keyframing on standard R15/R6 rigs will ensure fluid windup, contact, and recovery phases. Audio components sourced from Marketplace will be inspected and tested for proper playback timing.
spec.title: Strike Lab - Fighting Game Training Arena
spec.summary: Strike Lab is a single-player fighting game training arena designed for desktop and touch devices. Upon spawning in a sleek, minimalist training dojo arena, the player faces a humanoid training dummy positioned on a sparring ring. Players execute a 3-hit light attack combo (Jab, Cross, Roundhouse Kick) with clear telegraph/windup, active contact window, and recovery phases. The server strictly validates attack cadence, combo chaining timing, and spatial strike distance. Hits register damage and increment an accepted-hit counter exactly once during contact frames, while swings out of range or spamming during recovery produce distinct whiff/miss feedback without dealing damage or registering combo hits. When the dummy's health depletes, it plays a defeat reaction, pauses briefly, and automatically resets, while a dedicated manual reset button is also available in the HUD. The client provides intuitive desktop (M1/F key) and touch (on-screen Strike button) controls with live visual combo counters, dummy health bar, and floating combat text.
spec.visualDirection: High-contrast modern fighting gym/cyber-dojo aesthetic with clean neon arena bounds, dark carbon flooring, sparring boundary decals, and focused overhead studio spotlights. The training dummy stands centered on an elevated octagonal sparring pad with an overhead floating health bar and hit counter HUD. Attacks trigger distinct visual cues: punch trails and bright impact sparks on accepted contact, swift air whoosh effects on misses, and dynamic damage numbers bouncing upward.
